newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - DEC 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - DEC 27.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--President of the Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia Kiro Gligorov has called on Greece to stop pressing for a change in the fledgling state's name and to support "Republic of Macedonia" as the permanent name at UN-sponsored talks.
--EU Commissioner Christos Papoutsis denies that Greece's image in the eyes of Europe has improved and criticises the course taken by ruling party PASOK and the government over the last year.
--Perennial conservative opposition leadership contender George Souflias is reportedly preparing a new offensive against incumbent Miltiades Evert to kick off the New Year.
--A recent opinion poll in magazine 'Klik' has elected Prime Minister Costas Simitis man of the year but Athens Mayor Dimitris Avramopoulos most popular political figure.

--The holiday break has provided a short breathing space for a government facing three open fronts: farmers - who recently temporarily called off a 25-day blockade; the course of the economy, and particularly small and medium size enterprises; and education. On the other hand, the main opposition New Democracy continues to be buffeted by internal party squabbles.

--Democratic Social Movement leader Dimitris Tsovolas is confident that the political stage will definitively change in 1997 and that the government will have to deal with "uncontrollable" social reaction to its measures.
--In the depressed district of Keratsini, one of the power company DEH's pylons was transformed into the highest Christmas tree in the world.
--Christmas may not have been white but the next few days will see heavy snowfall and a sharp drop in temperatures around the country.
--Teenage gang members around Athens will be charged after they stole money gathered from carolling on Christmas Eve. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
